primary_source: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th ed. (printed page numbers)
lookup_rule: Sp: among grade rows whose size range contains d, use the lowest priority number (1 = Shigley, 2 = standard), preferring rows whose scope covers the thread. A fine-pitch thread below a row's fine_pitch_d_min still uses that row, flagged with fine_pitch_note.
fine_pitch_note: {source} covers fine pitch from M8 x 1 only. The class value is applied to this thread by extension: verify with the supplier or enter Sp.

shigley.citation: Budynas & Nisbett, Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th ed., McGraw-Hill, Chapter 8

iso_898_1.citation: ISO 898-1:2013, Mechanical properties of fasteners made of carbon steel and alloy steel - Part 1: Bolts, screws and studs, Table 3 (row 5, stress under proof load Sp,nom) and Clause 1 (scope)
iso_898_1.verification: Table 3 and scope read in the official ISO preview.

iso_3506_1.citation: ISO 3506-1:2020, Fasteners - Mechanical properties of corrosion-resistant stainless steel fasteners - Part 1: Bolts, screws and studs, Clause 1 (scope) and austenitic property-class table (Rm, Rp0.2)
iso_3506_1.verification: Scope (M1.6-M39 coarse, M8x1-M39x3 fine) read in the ISO preview. The property table is not in the free preview; Rp0.2 values confirmed in three published reproductions (BSSA SSAS 2.31, Andrews Fasteners, Boltport). The 2020 edition tabulates class 70/80 loads up to M39; the 2009 edition limited classes 70/80 to M24 (BSSA).
iso_3506_1.note: Bolts, screws and studs have no proof stress in ISO 3506-1 (only nuts do), so Sp = 0.85*Sy per Shigley p. 434.

iso_261.citation: ISO 261:1998, ISO general purpose metric screw threads - General plan, Table 2 (nominal diameter/pitch)
iso_261.verification: Table 2 read in full in the official ISO preview.

asme_b1_1.citation: ASME B1.1, Unified Inch Screw Threads (UN and UNR thread form)
asme_b1_1.verification: UNEF sizes/TPI confirmed in two ASME B1.1 data charts (efunda, ring-plug-thread-gages). 1-1/8 and 1-3/8 UNC/UNF TPI confirmed in ASTM A574-04e1 Tables 2-3 and the Wikipedia UTS table. Numbered-size diameter formula confirmed in the Wikipedia UTS article and matches every diameter in Shigley Table 8-2.

astm_a574.citation: ASTM A574, Standard Specification for Alloy Steel Socket-Head Cap Screws (checked in A574-04e1), Tables 2-3, footnote C: proof load (length measurement method) based on 140 ksi for 0.500 in and smaller, 135 ksi for larger; scope 0.060-4 in
astm_a574.verification: Read in a copy of ASTM A574-04e1; same values in the current Baden Steel summary.

astm_f593.citation: ASTM F593, Standard Specification for Stainless Steel Bolts, Hex Cap Screws, and Studs: Groups 1 and 2, condition CW (furnished unless otherwise specified); CW1 1/4-5/8 in, CW2 3/4-1-1/2 in; scope 1/4-1-1/2 in
astm_f593.verification: Yield strengths, size ranges and default condition confirmed in three published summaries. F593 gives tensile and yield only, no proof load, so Sp = 0.85*Sy per Shigley p. 434.

astm_f837.citation: ASTM F837-20, Standard Specification for Stainless Steel Socket Head Cap Screws, Table 1: Groups 1 and 2, condition CW (yield 40 ksi min) and CW1 (yield 65 ksi min), 0.060-0.750 in; scope 0.060-1.500 in
astm_f837.verification: Table 1 read in the ASTM F837-20 redline (vs F837-13(2018)); same values in the Torqbolt summary. F837 gives machined-specimen yield but no proof load, so Sp = 0.85*Sy per Shigley p. 434. F837 names no default condition (Sec. 4.1.4: the order must state it).

sae_j429.citation: SAE J429, Mechanical and Material Requirements for Externally Threaded Fasteners
sae_j429.verification: Grades 2, 5, 8 proof loads confirmed; used only as a cross-check of Shigley Table 8-9.

nasa_std_5020b.citation: NASA-STD-5020B (approved 2021-08-06), Requirements for Threaded Fastening Systems in Spaceflight Hardware, Sec. 4.3.3 [TFSR 7], Table 3 'Preload Variation Determination' and Appendix A.2

lubrication_notes.always: K assumes lubricant on BOTH the threads and the under-head bearing face.
lubrication_notes.no_preselect: No lubricant is pre-selected: the choice moves preload by up to 2.5x.

finish_hints.black-oxide: Black-oxide screws often ship lightly oiled. Choose Dry if degreased, Lubricated if as-received.
finish_hints.zinc-plated: Zinc-plated: Shigley Table 8-15 gives K = 0.20 as received. Choose Lubricated if you oil them.
finish_hints.other: Shigley gives no K for this finish. Use vendor data (Custom) or pick the closest condition.

engagement.label: Tapped aluminum or other soft material
Free-running helical insert
notes: K depends on insert coating and wear.

engagement.label: Screw-locking helical insert
engagement.running_torque_prompt: Run the screw in with a torque wrench and record the torque just before the head seats.

reused_insert.note: K changes as inserts are reused: in NASA tests it rose with repeated cycles for dry installs and fell for lubricated installs (NASA NTRS 20150004064, pp. 235 and 242). Re-check torque-tension for reused inserts.
reused_insert.spec_text: K tends to rise as inserts wear (NASA NTRS 20150004064).
reused_insert.spec_text_note: The paper reports a rise only for dry (unlubricated) installs; lubricated installs trended down.

gamma_policy.clause: NASA-STD-5020B Sec. 4.3.3 [TFSR 7], Table 3; Appendix A.2 (same in NASA-STD-5020A w/Change 1)
gamma_policy.applicability: Torque control, non-separation-critical joints, alternate (non-statistical) method. These are floors: use the larger test-measured variation if you have one. Separation-critical joints need a statistical basis from lot-specific tests.
gamma_policy.lubricated_definition: Lubricated means a solid-film, grease or liquid lubricant on the threads AND the turning bearing surface (NASA-STD-5020B Sec. 4.3.3).

shigley_scatter.description: Preload scatter at equal torque (1/2-20 UNF bolts, 800 lbf-in, reported in SI as 90 N-m)
